title: Topic 7.4: Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers

pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 7.4.1 CHARACTERS IN CLASS READERS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can you tell the difference between a main and a minor character in a story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify minor characters in a text
2. discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify minor characters in a text
   In simple words: practise until you can identify minor characters in a text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text
   In simple words: practise until you can discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers.
4. Show that you can: identify minor characters in a text

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read and identify minor characters in a class reader,
2. Discuss how the characters relate with each other,
3. Critical thinking: It is developed as the learner links the relationships between characters in the class reader.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you tell the difference between a main and a minor character in a story?
2. How would you describe the behaviour of your classmates?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify minor characters in a text
2. discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
